title: Microsoft Research introduces StudentSim for AI tutor evaluation
excerpt: The research system uses personalized simulators to provide feedback on AI tutoring tools before they are tested with real students.
bodyHtml:
Microsoft Research announced StudentSim on October 12, 2026, a research system designed to evaluate and improve AI tutoring tools. The system creates personalized simulators of individual students by training on publicly available, de-identified learner records to model how students respond to tutor guidance.

The research includes StudentSimEval, a benchmark protocol covering chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics. The system uses a two-stage training pipeline, first learning shared student behavior from pooled records before specializing on one student’s own records.

In testing, a tutor trained with StudentSim feedback reached 90.5% accuracy, compared to 75.7% for a baseline model without reinforcement learning. The tutor also received higher ratings for guidance quality and personalization. The research team has made the StudentSim training and evaluation code publicly available.
topic: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
